qualification_observations: Sixty-six new real-session/CSRF tests reject invalid table references, oversized/conflicting identifiers and unverified/mismatched model overrides before readers run. They also cover valid managed references, external output directory symlinks, forced upload/encoding collisions, metadata failure and ambiguous legacy fallback.

Existing development-only native explanation tests now exercise relative/absolute verified model overrides without an active projection. Sealed final evidence is deliberately unreadable; all three variants succeed using development rows.

An initial mixed explicit pytest argument order omitted the child-directory autouse handler fixture, producing seven authentication failures. Retained diagnostics identified the missing fixture. Parent-first focused collection and standard full collection passed; runtime authentication was unchanged.

Four new authenticated browser/API scenarios exercise blocked references/identifiers/model overrides and preserved repeated upload/encoding files with metadata downloads. The prior nineteen governed workflows and actual MCP stdio operator workflow passed on the same executable source.

Scientific datasets, round counts, timeout/assertion, skip and coverage budgets were preserved. The six full-suite skips require four optional installed SDK checks, a live model engine and a local .env.
limits: A managed-root check is not dataset/project authorization. Signed-in REST users still have installation-wide access; MCP uses its separate installation actor/grants.
The controller/filesystem are trusted; path resolution is not a sandbox or filesystem-race defense against a hostile local process.
Expert Python remains blocked. Exact action approvals, gVisor isolation, expert transformations/scorers and replay/scoring remain unimplemented.

Verified client-selected native XGBoost overrides do not certify all legacy/internal fitted-state readers or historical provenance. Ambiguous legacy matches return no file; historical files are preserved.

UUID names and exclusive file creation prevent overwrite; they do not provide a transaction across database/filesystem, durable recovery or full immutable versioning of legacy stages. A failed metadata write may leave an unpublished partial sidecar, but no success or CSV publication.
Project roles, policy/retention/egress, independent reproduction, PostgreSQL/durable jobs and release/customer/value qualification remain open. D18-D26 and canonical queue are preserved.

workspace_preservation.scope: Managed worktree and disposable test services only; primary configuration/running stack preserved. Per-command hooks disabled because they target primary containers; equivalent independent checks passed and persistent Git config is unchanged.
